18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
COUNCILMEMBER VO WILL PARTICIPATE VIA TELECONFERENCE FROM 17702 OWEN AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703, AND THIS AGENDA WILL BE POSTED AT THAT LOCATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 9,
2023, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA. COUNCILMEMBER VO PARTICIPATED VIA
TELECONFERENCE FROM 17702 OWEN AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703, AND THE MEETING
AGENDA WAS POSTED AT THAT LOCATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CALIFORNIA
GOVERNMENT CODE.

 1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

 2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Jeff Ludington, Generations Church.

 3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by the Panthers – Cerritos Youth Flag Football Team
  (Intermediate Division).

 4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Chuong Vo (via teleconference)
  Council/Agency Member Frank Aurelio Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Bruce W. Barrows

 5.  Presentations/Appointments

 5A.  Presentations

  None.

 5B.  Review and consideration of appointments, removals, and filling of scheduled or unscheduled
  vacancies on the Cerritos Advisory Boards (2022-24 term) (COUNCIL).

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  There were no public comments received on this item and no action was taken.

 6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written Correspondence:
  (Written correspondence submitted by the deadline listed on the agenda is considered
  public record. Prior to the meeting, the Council/Agency received copies of the full-text
  unredacted written correspondence that was submitted for this item. Public requests for
  copies of the full-text redacted written correspondence can be made during regular
  business hours to the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer.)

  Ijya Karki requested that Council consider returning to the hybrid public meeting format to
  allow for virtual public participation.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the Mayor
  declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Thursday, October 26, 2023, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting
  Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Johnson, to approve the Thursday,
  October 26, 2023, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of Register of Demands

7B.1. Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated November 9, 2023 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Johnson, to approve the Register of
  Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  November 9, 2023  $9,564,112.19 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of the Treasurer’s Reports

  City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer's Reports for the period ending September 30,
  2023 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Johnson, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending September 30, 2023
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7D.  Award of contract for parts and services to repair Herman Miller Classic Aeron Chairs at the
  Cerritos Library, Bid No. 1527-23 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Johnson, to award a contract to Pivot
  Interiors, Inc. in the amount of $19,862.95 for parts and services to repair Herman Miller
  Classic Aeron Chairs at the Cerritos Library (total bid) and reject the other bids (COUNCIL).

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7D.  (continued)

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of renaming three of the Cerritos Library Study Rooms for Marie
  Curie, Katherine Johnson, and Chien-Shiung Wu (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian and Marketing Manager.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to direct staff to:

  1. Order new Study Rooms signs from TFN Architectural Signage for the names of the top
  three (3) vote-getters in the Cerritos Library Study Room Names Voting Survey, including
  Marie Curie, Katherine Johnson, and Chien-Shiung Wu;

  2. Conduct an online survey for the community to vote for the three (3) male names to
  remain in place for Cerritos Library Study Rooms; and

  3. Replace and install signs, as applicable, and update the Study Room names listed on
  the Cerritos Library’s website and on the Study Room reservations confirmation slips
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of an informational budget and audit compliance report for Fiscal
  Year 2023-24 (COUNCIL).

  Staff reports were given by Peter Kemp, Budget Manager and Amandeep Mann, Associate
  Civil Engineer. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Yokoyama, to ratify the executed
  Budget Amendments from the first quarter of Fiscal Year 2023-2024 as summarized in the
  Budget Adjustment Log (Exhibit 1) of the agenda report associated with this item
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Yokoyama, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  OF CERRITOS AMENDING SECTION 2.04 (STRATEGIC FINANCIAL PLAN AND BUDGET
  PREPARATION POLICY) OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS POLICY AND PROCEDURE MANUAL
  RELATED TO SCHEDULING OF MEETINGS AND OTHER SCHEDULING REQUIREMENTS
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Peter Kemp, Budget Manager.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Barrows, to refer review of the proposed
  amendments to the City Strategic Financial Plan and Budget Preparation Policy (2.04) to the
  Policy and Procedure ad hoc working group and return their recommendations to the City
  Council for consideration (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 – 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Vo, Solanki, Barrows
  NOES:  Johnson, Yokoyama
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or Federal
  legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  Reports

11A.  Report from City Manager/Executive Director

  None.

11B.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports

  Reports were given by Councilmembers Johnson and Yokoyama, and Mayor Pro Tem
  Solanki.

  Councilmember Johnson submitted a document for the record entitled, “Supporting
  Operation Green Light for Veterans.” (Documents submitted during the meeting are
  considered public record and can be requested at the Office of the City Clerk during regular
  business hours.)

  CONSENSUS (Johnson): Directed the City Manager to schedule an agenda report at a
  future meeting for City Council consideration of the “Operation Green Light for Veterans”
  resolution.

12.  Closed Session

  Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, announced the City Council would recess to Closed Session to
  discuss Items 12A and 12B, as listed on the Closed Session agenda.

  12A.  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS

  12B.  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957.6 (COUNCIL)
  Agency Negotiators: Robert A. Lopez, City Manager, Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, and
  Patricia Leyva, Personnel/Risk Manager
  Unrepresented Employees: Full-Time Exempt

  The City Council recessed into Closed Session.

  The City Council reconvened into Open Session.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT:

  Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, provided the following Closed Session report:

  The City Council convened into Closed Session to discuss Items 12A and 12B as listed on
  the agenda. There was no reportable action taken on either item and there was nothing
  further to report.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 9:30 p.m. in memory of Ethan Soriano.
